intent: Increase vegetation/natural complexity through maintained root-zone planting interfaces and cause-based low understory while preserving the benchmark's ordinary midsummer Japanese residential-estate character.

assemblies.establishment: Four tree anchors touch the plaza paving footprint. One ring is fully pavement-supported; three sit on a plaza/lawn boundary and therefore require the curb modules to follow their actual local support grade rather than hover at one world height.
assemblies.nominalDimensions: final exposed-soil opening diameter 2.30 m; radius 1.15 m sized from the generated mature root-flare envelope; 12 edging modules; edging section 150 x 80 mm; approximately 12 mm tangential dry joints
assemblies.materialsFinish: dry mineral topsoil with compacted fine aggregate; matte non-metallic precast concrete edging with small physical chamfers; root bark remains a rough dielectric
assemblies.mounting: the root-zone visual volume extends below the lower lawn datum so its underside cannot become visible; paving-supported curb modules embed 8 mm and lawn-supported modules embed 6 mm. The intended soil construction datum is flush/slightly recessed, while the retained coarse collision slab requires only a 1.5 mm positive visual separation that must be invisible at native 4K.
assemblies.interfaces: generated root flare -> exposed soil with at least 90 mm contracted clearance -> inner curb face -> 12 mm module joint -> locally supported plaza paving or lawn; no unexplained painted contact ring or floating curb is allowed
assemblies.orientationExposure: upward-facing, rain/sun exposed, with three boundary rings following the approximately 50 mm plaza-to-lawn grade change and one interior ring fully supported by paving
assemblies.aging: ordinary compaction, circulation-side soil wear, mild soil darkening near the trunk and slight concrete aggregate exposure are permitted only where caused by use/exposure; arbitrary damage cues are not used
assemblies.geometryVsMaterial: opening radius, root clearance, soil volume, curb height/embed, module joints and support-grade steps are geometry; soil grain, bark fissure, concrete pores and ordinary UV/roughness variation remain material detail
assemblies.lodPolicy: root flares remain through tree LOD0/1/2/3; tree-pit substrate and edging remain static construction geometry; added biological understory uses explicit LOD0/1/2/3
assemblies.lookdevBrief: At oblique 100 percent crop, roots must remain inside the exposed root zone without entering curb/paving, every curb module must bear on its local pavement/lawn grade, and the 1.5 mm fallback separation must not read as a raised brown slab. Grazing light should reveal real curb chamfers/joints rather than baked highlights.

assemblies.establishment: Sparse spontaneous/maintained low vegetation establishes within the root zone. Density is reduced toward the nearest pedestrian-pressure source and remains denser on protected sides instead of being distributed uniformly.
assemblies.nominalDimensions: plant height 0.18-0.42 m; leaf-rosette spread approximately 0.20-0.36 m at LOD0; paved pits use 7-9 source plants while grass-ground trees use 16-22 source plants before LOD reduction
assemblies.materialsFinish: thin dielectric foliage using the existing two-sided foliage transmission model; small green stems reuse non-metallic foliage material
assemblies.mounting: paved-pit plant origins are reset to 1 mm above the final root-zone soil visual surface and grass-tree origins to 4 mm above the lawn datum so finite-radius stem geometry penetrates its support instead of floating
assemblies.interfaces: root-zone soil/grass -> stem -> leaf spray; circulation-facing sector has lower occupancy due to ordinary foot traffic/maintenance pressure
assemblies.orientationExposure: midsummer sun/sky context from the existing deterministic environment; individual rosettes have deterministic yaw and modest pitch variation
assemblies.aging: ordinary summer growth with modest size/color variation only
assemblies.geometryVsMaterial: stem direction, rosette silhouette, spacing, physical root datum and LOD reduction are explicit geometry; leaf vein/color and transmitted-light response are material/shader detail
assemblies.lodPolicy: four renderer-distinct levels with animated cross-fade; plant population is progressively reduced and stems are removed after LOD1; visible LOD pop is an automatic fail
assemblies.lookdevBrief: Close view should reveal independent low plants with stem bases entering soil/grass, not hovering above it. Oblique view should show lower circulation-side occupancy; far view must collapse smoothly without shimmer or a sudden green ring.

materials.albedoGuidance: dry warm-brown mineral soil; no baked lighting or black contact-shadow halo
materials.normalScaleGuidance: fine soil/aggregate microrelief only; root-zone volume/opening remains geometric
materials.microstructure: fine mineral grains, small aggregate and compaction variation
materials.wetnessResponse: not active in the dry benchmark; any later wet variant must follow physical catchment and contact logic
materials.uvAging: no UV hue shift beyond mild ordinary summer desaturation
materials.angularFresnelResponse: weak dielectric grazing reflection; never metallic

materials.albedoGuidance: neutral aged precast concrete without painted edge highlights
materials.normalScaleGuidance: small aggregate and pores; 80 mm section, support-grade step and chamfer are geometry
materials.microstructure: washed/aged cement paste with visible fine aggregate
materials.wetnessResponse: dry benchmark only; any future wet state must be source/catchment based
materials.uvAging: small exposure-driven lightening permitted, no stylized bleaching
materials.angularFresnelResponse: broad subdued dielectric grazing response created by real illumination

materials.albedoGuidance: midsummer green foliage with cluster-level variation; no emissive green
materials.normalScaleGuidance: leaf micro-normal/vein response from the existing foliage material
materials.microstructure: thin leaf lamina with vein-scale normal variation
materials.wetnessResponse: dry benchmark; no generic wet sheen
materials.angularFresnelResponse: two-sided dielectric leaf response with modest transmission under coherent midsummer sun

tree-pit curb module visibly floats above its local pavement/lawn support
root-zone soil reveals an unsupported underside
understory stems visibly float above their support surface
uniform circular/stamped understory distribution immediately obvious at benchmark framing
visible Unity primitive mesh in ecology detail
claiming vegetation visual quality without an actual Unity render
